stem: Consider the graph of the parent function y = sin x on the interval 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π. Which list gives the points on this graph at x = 0, π/2, π, 3π/2, and 2π, in that order?

choices.rationale: This swaps sine and cosine. These are the anchor points of y = cos x, which starts at its maximum, but sin 0 = 0, so the sine graph starts at the origin. Fix: Evaluate sin 0 first and check whether the graph starts at 0 or at 1.

This puts the extrema in the wrong quarter-periods, so the graph dips first. Since sin(π/2) = 1 and sin(3π/2) = −1, sine rises to its maximum before it reaches its minimum. Fix: Find the unit-circle point at π/2 and read its y-coordinate to set the first extremum.

This treats sine as never negative. On (π, 2π) the unit-circle point lies below the x-axis, so sine is negative there, and the range of sine is [−1, 1]. Fix: Check the sign of the y-coordinate at 3π/2 on the unit circle before you plot it.
Sine is the y-coordinate on the unit circle. It starts at 0, rises to its maximum 1 at π/2, returns to 0 at π, and falls to its minimum −1 at 3π/2. It returns to 0 at 2π, completing one period.
